extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners/processing staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner/applicant procedures governing filing dates, conversions between provisional and nonprovisional applications, missing specification pages/drawings/claims, required fees/cover sheets, and related petitions and notices under 35 U.S.C. and 37 CFR (as explained in MPEP § 601.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application filing date (post-December 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application filed on or after December 18, 2013 will be given a filing date as of the date a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For provisional applications filed prior to December 18, 2013, filing date is given per pre-PLT (AIA) 37 CFR 1.53(c) as of the date the written description and any necessary drawings are filed. Amendments, other than those required to make the provisional application comply with applicable regulations, are not permitted after the filing date of the provisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application cover sheet requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(c)(1) requires all provisional applications be filed with a cover sheet, which may be an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or a cover letter identifying the application as a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will treat an application as filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) unless the application is clearly identified as a provisional application. A provisional identified as such but lacking a complete cover sheet (as required by 37 CFR 1.51(c)(1)) will be treated as a provisional application; the complete cover sheet and a surcharge must be submitted later in conformance with 37 CFR 1.53(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing cover sheet or filing fee procedure for provisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: When the provisional application does not have a complete cover sheet or the appropriate fee, the applicant will be notified pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53(g) and given a time period in which to provide the necessary fee or cover sheet and to pay the surcharge as set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(g) in order to avoid abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time period will usually be two months from the date of notification and may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If the filing fee is not timely paid, the Office may dispose of the provisional application. If no correspondence address has been provided, applicant has two months from the filing date to file the basic filing fee and pay the surcharge. Copies of a provisional application will be provided by the USPTO upon request and payment of the fee in 37 CFR 1.19(b) unless the provisional application has been disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing fee requirement for provisional benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic filing fee must be paid in a provisional application on filing or within the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.53(g), and the provisional application must be entitled to a filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(c), if any claim for benefits under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) based on that application is made in a subsequently filed nonprovisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to review refusal to accord filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(e)(2) requires that any request for review of a refusal to accord an application a filing date be made by way of a petition accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 506.02 for petition practice and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from a nonprovisional application to a provisional application (37 CFR 1.53(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent filed under paragraph (b) may be converted to a provisional application and be accorded the original filing date of the application filed under paragraph (b). The request for conversion must be accompanied by the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(q) and be filed prior to abandonment, payment of the issue fee, or expiration of twelve months after the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant of such a request will not entitle applicant to a refund of fees properly paid in the original application. The provisional application filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(d)) and the surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(g)) are also required though need not be paid with the request; if not paid, the Office will send a Notice to File Missing Parts requiring these fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication consequences of converting to provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting a nonprovisional application to a provisional application will not avoid the publication of the nonprovisional application unless the request to convert is recognized in sufficient time to permit the officials to remove the nonprovisional application from the publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office cannot ensure removal or avoidance of publication once the publication process has been initiated. For procedures to remove an application from publication, see MPEP § 1120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional applications cannot claim priority/benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application is not entitled to claim priority to or benefit of a prior-filed application under 35 U.S.C. 119, 120, 121, 365, or 386.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a nonprovisional application has been converted to a provisional application, any priority or benefit claims submitted in the nonprovisional application will be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from a provisional to a nonprovisional application (37 CFR 1.53(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional application and accorded the original filing date of the provisional. The conversion must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(i) and an amendment including at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b), unless the provisional application otherwise contains at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resulting nonprovisional must also include the filing fee, search fee, and examination fee for a nonprovisional application, and the surcharge required by § 1.16(f) if either the basic filing fee for a nonprovisional application or the inventor's oath or declaration was not present on the filing date accorded the resulting nonprovisional application. The request must be filed prior to abandonment or expiration of 12 months after the provisional filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term consequences of converting provisional to nonprovisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of a provisional application to a nonprovisional application will result in the term of any patent to issue from the application being measured from at least the filing date of the provisional application for which conversion is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider avoiding adverse patent term impact by filing a nonprovisional claiming the benefit of the provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), rather than converting the provisional to a nonprovisional. Claiming benefit is less expensive and will generally result in a longer patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requests for conversion by mail
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who wish to file a request for conversion under 37 CFR 1.53(c)(2) or (c)(3) by mail should designate “Mail Stop Conversion” as part of the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office address.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP handling of applications filed without all pages of specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) reviews application papers to determine whether all of the pages of specification are present. If the application, though missing pages, contains something that can be construed as a written description, at least one drawing figure if necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 (first sentence), and, in a nonprovisional application, at least one claim, OPAP will send a Notice of Omitted Items indicating that the application papers have been accorded a filing date but are lacking some pages of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application does not contain anything that can be construed as a written description, OPAP will mail a Notice of Incomplete Application indicating the application lacks the specification required by 35 U.S.C. 112 and no filing date is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant options after OPAP Notice of Omitted Items (entitled to filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the revised procedure, the mailing of an OPAP notice regarding missing page(s) will permit the applicant to: (A) promptly establish prior receipt by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) within two months with the petition fee and evidence; (B) promptly submit the omitted page(s) and accept the date of such submission as the application filing date by filing omitted pages and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 within two months; or (C) accept the application as deposited by filing an appropriate amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For option C, acceptable amendments include: (1) substitute specification (including claims) to renumber pages and cancel incomplete sentences without adding subject matter (37 CFR 1.121(b)(3), 1.125); or (2) substitute specification (excluding claims) relying on incorporation by reference under 37 CFR 1.57(b) to add subject matter in omitted pages without adding new matter. The two-month period is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136. For provisional applications, petition practice under 1.182 is generally not granted; the USPTO suggests filing a new provisional application instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when applicant accepts application as deposited
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant accepts the application as deposited by filing an appropriate amendment, the application will maintain the filing date as of the date of deposit of the application papers in the USPTO, and the original application papers will include only those papers present in the USPTO on the date of deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must not add new matter (35 U.S.C. 132(a)). For omitted page(s) of the claim listing, applicant must submit replacement claim listing with claims renumbered consecutively, or a complete claim listing per 37 CFR 1.121(c) if claim amendments are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: If application is not entitled to a filing date (missing specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application lacks the specification required by 35 U.S.C. 112 and is not entitled to a filing date, the applicant may: (A) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with the petition fee asserting missing specification was submitted or that papers contain an adequate written description and submit evidence; (B) submit the omitted specification (including at least one claim if required) and accept the date of such submission as the filing date; or (C) submit an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(b) if the omitted material is completely contained in a prior-filed application (with petition under 1.53(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, omitted specification submissions should be accompanied by an oath or declaration in compliance with pre-AIA rules referring to the specification. The two-month period for some responses is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties when forwarded an application missing specification pages
rubrics_metrics.description: If a forwarded application was filed without all of the pages of the specification and a Notice of Omitted Items has not been mailed by OPAP, the examiner should review the application to determine whether the application is entitled to a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: For an application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) prior to December 18, 2013 or a design application, it is entitled to a filing date if it contains something that can be construed as a written description, at least one drawing figure (if necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113), and at least one claim. For non-design applications filed on or after December 18, 2013 under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), the application is entitled to a filing date if filed with a specification, with or without claims (though claims must be filed before sent to the Technology Center). If entitled, the examiner should notify applicant in the next Office action and require applicant to take specified actions (accept as filed with amendment, submit omitted pages + petition, or file petition alleging prior deposit). If not entitled, forward to OPAP for Notice of Incomplete Application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional applications filed without at least one claim (pre-December 18, 2013 and design apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonprovisional applications filed prior to December 18, 2013 or design applications, a claim is a statutory requirement for according a filing date to the application. If such an application does not contain at least one claim, a 'Notice of Incomplete Application' will be mailed indicating no filing date has been granted and setting a period for submitting a claim. The filing date will be the date of receipt of at least one claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments that cancel all claims without presenting any new or substitute claims will be disapproved; the application will not be denied a filing date merely because such a preliminary amendment was submitted on filing. For fee calculation purposes, the Office will treat such an application as containing only a single claim. An alternative for some applicants is to petition to convert the 111(a) application to a 111(b) application under 37 CFR 1.53(c)(2) prior to expiration of 12 months after deposit, which avoids the claim requirement for initial filing date (where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications filed without drawings (drawing necessity and filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 113 requires a drawing 'where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter sought to be patented.' For applications filed prior to December 18, 2013 and design applications, required drawings (where necessary) are needed to receive a filing date. For applications other than design filed on or after December 18, 2013, drawings are not required to receive a filing date though they should be submitted if necessary for understanding because no amendment may introduce new matter after filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed without drawings are inspected to determine whether a drawing is referred to in the specification, and if not, whether a drawing is necessary. USPTO practice treats at least process/method claims and many composition applications as not requiring drawings. Specific situations usually not requiring drawings include: (A) coated articles or products where invention is solely coating; (B) articles made from a particular material where only material matters; (C) laminated structures unless significant structure details; (D) articles/apparatus/systems where sole distinguishing feature is presence of a particular material. If the Technology Center determines drawings are necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113, filing date will be reconsidered and application returned to OPAP for a Notice of Incomplete Application. If drawings are described in the specification but not filed, treated as filed without all drawing figures and handled per MPEP § 601.01(g).
